mechanism_narrative: The sharp concurrent drops in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicate fewer commuting trips and fewer discretionary stops near job centers, which will continue to depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages above its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay below their current 4-week means.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week surge in RESIDENTIAL time relative to baseline means people substitute away from outside shopping and dining, so RETAIL_REC falls further within the next week as stay-at-home behavior deepens.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w RESIDENTIAL is 3.0 after 0.6 the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the next 7 days after RESIDENTIAL exceeds +2 and instead rises above its prior 7-day level.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall together, the joint reduction in weekday mobility suppresses unplanned retail visits, so RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series are negative at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below zero or continue falling.

mechanism_narrative: A steep decline in PARKS mobility marks an active distancing or closure regime that spills over into shopping trips, producing a lower RETAIL_REC level over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w PARKS is -5.1 after -0.6 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline within 14 days after PARKS crosses below -5 and instead moves above its preceding 14-day average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM signals stockpiling and replacement of restaurant or retail trips with essential shopping, which should pull RETAIL_REC down over the following month.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w GROCERY_PHARM is 9.3, the highest value in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining elevated.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS stays below its recent average while TRANSIT stays deeply negative, leisure demand is being pulled indoors and away from mixed-use destinations, which will keep RETAIL_REC below the prior four-week mean over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not stay below its prior 14-day average over the next 14 days even though PARKS and TRANSIT remain depressed.

mechanism_narrative: Once WORKPLACES turns negative after a prior near-zero week, it indicates a fresh contraction in on-site activity that should reduce retail footfall with a one-week lag.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES crosses from at or above 0 to below 0
evidence_refs: fact:t-2w and t-1w were near zero, then t-0w fell to -4.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week after WORKPLACES crosses below zero and instead exceeds its prior week level.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises while TRANSIT falls, people are shifting time to home and reducing out-of-home trips, which will lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w RESIDENTIAL is 3.0 and TRANSIT is -14.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL remains above +2 and TRANSIT remains below -10.
